question: For what value of \(x\) does \(10^x\cdot 100^{2x}=1000^5?\)
solution:
The numbers \(10\), \(100\), and \(1000\) are powers of the same base, so rewriting them makes their exponents comparable. Since \(100=10^2\) and \(1000=10^3\), the equation becomes
\[
10^x(10^2)^{2x}=(10^3)^5,
\]
and hence
\[
10^{x+4x}=10^{15},\qquad 10^{5x}=10^{15}.
\]
All bases are positive, so the power laws apply for every real \(x\). Powers of \(10\) strictly increase with their exponents, so equal powers have equal exponents. Therefore \(5x=15\), giving the unique solution \(x=3\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
